To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Episodic medical home care interventions are effective for improving quality of life and reducing hospitalization rates in severe bedridden patients with chronic respiratory failure; (2) the medical home model is an effective way to provide care for patients with severe bedridden chronic illness; (3) the medical home is a cost-effective way to provide care to patients with severe chronic illness.

The episodic medical home (EMH) model is an effective and safe alternative to the traditional medical home (TMH) model for severe chronic respiratory failure (CRF) patients who are bedridden for at least 50% of their time.

The episodic medical home intervention in severe bedridden patients with chronic respiratory failure (CRF) was associated with significant reduction in the number of hospital admissions, hospitalization days, hospitalization days per admission, hospitalization costs, emergency room (ER) visits, and ER costs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the episodic medical home (EMH) model on the care of severe chronic respiratory failure (CRF) patients in the last year of their life.
the effects of a 4-year medical home intervention on a group of patients suffering from severe bedridden chronic lung disease.
the development of an innovative, low-cost, and easy-to-use device for the monitoring of patients with chronic respiratory failure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the medical home is not a panacea for all that ails the American health care system, but that it is a useful tool that, when implemented correctly, can improve health outcomes and reduce costs.
the use of the episodic medical home model for severe bedridden chronic patients with respiratory failure is not only feasible, but also beneficial for the patients and their families.
the use of a medical home model for patients with severe chronic respiratory failure is associated with a reduction of hospital admissions and a decrease in the number of hospital days.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the episodic medical home intervention (EMHI) is an effective and safe method for the treatment of severe bedridden chronic patients.
we have shown that a medical home intervention can improve the quality of life in severe chronic respiratory failure patients.
we have developed a novel model of care for patients with severe bedridden chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and chronic respiratory failure (CRF).
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need more research on the effectiveness of the Episodic Medical Home (EMH) model.
the medical home model can be used to improve care coordination and outcomes in a vulnerable population of chronic respiratory failure patients.
we can use the medical home as a framework to improve the health and well-being of patients with advanced chronic respiratory failure.
